quotes.text: Events are lightweight. They carry just enough information to tell you something happened and where to look. They don't carry the full payload.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in one breath the key difference between an event and a message.

quotes.text: The publisher doesn't know the subscribers and the subscribers don't know the publisher. They just trust Event Grid to route the message correctly.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the decoupling principle behind publish-subscribe routing.

quotes.text: Dead lettering is your safety net. You configure a storage location, usually a storage queue or a blob storage container. If all retries fail, event grid moves the event to that dead letter location.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, practical explanation of how undeliverable events are preserved.

quotes.text: Here's a simple rule to remember. Event grid reacts. Event hubs streams. Service bus coordinates.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable rule of thumb for choosing between Azure's three messaging services.

quotes.text: Move from polling to event driven. Stop wasting compute and bandwidth on empty checks. Start building reactive systems that only do work when there's actual work to do.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core recommendation as an actionable principle.

chapters.title: Event Grid as the smart home hub
Event Grid vs Event Hubs vs Service Bus

takeaways: Event Grid replaces wasteful polling with push-based, event-driven reactions, and you pay per event rather than for idle infrastructure.
Events are lightweight notifications published to system or custom topics, then routed by filtered subscriptions to handlers such as Azure Functions, Logic Apps, webhooks or queues.
Retries with exponential back-off and dead-lettering keep events from disappearing, and Event Grid complements rather than replaces Event Hubs and Service Bus.
hook: Many systems still waste compute and bandwidth asking 'anything new yet?' over and over. This episode explains Azure Event Grid in plain English for cloud architects and developers, using a smart home analogy to show how events, topics, subscriptions, filtering and dead-lettering let services react instantly instead of polling.
